clue.text: Present probably was oddly wide, outside paper being crumpled

indicators.note: outside says those two letters sit around the other piece, one either side
oddly asks for the odd-numbered letters of the word wide, its first and third
paper that is crumpled is pushed out of shape, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone recalls a gift whose odd wide parcel had its paper all scrunched up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Present probably' is an adjective-like hint: a present is likely to have been covered in paper. 'oddly' picks letters one and three of wide.
explanation.definitionFit: A present is usually covered in gift paper, so the clue's 'probably' hedges an example.

clue.text: Argument about vessel's treasure

indicators.note: about means the word is turned round

parts.note: a row is an argument
a ship is a vessel

explanation.surface: A dispute over a ship's cargo of riches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns ROW into WOR. 'treasure' is a verb here, not the cargo.
explanation.definitionFit: To treasure someone is to adore or revere them, a verb meaning to adore.

clue.text: Country — not a large country

indicators.note: not means those letters are taken away

parts.note: Australia is a country
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: A small European nation described as not being a big one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' removes A and L from AUSTRALIA. A solver may confuse the two countries; the wordplay separates them.
explanation.definitionFit: Austria is a landlocked nation in central Europe.

clue.text: Rest feet, by the sound of it

indicators.note: by the sound of it says the word is identified by how it is spoken

parts.note: paws are animals' feet

explanation.surface: Advice to put one's feet up for a while.
explanation.definitionFit: A pause is a short rest or break in activity.

clue.text: Separates Germany and Italy's viewpoints

parts.note: D is the international vehicle code for Germany
I is the international vehicle code for Italy
stances are positions or viewpoints

explanation.surface: Germany and Italy's differing positions drive them apart.
explanation.definitionFit: To distance people is to keep them apart, so the verb means separates.

clue.text: Made out tit, unfortunately, being swallowed by another bird

indicators.note: being swallowed means one piece goes inside the body of another

parts.note: the wren is a small common bird

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests things went wrong for the tit, so its letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A small tit meets a grim end inside a larger bird, as described in a report.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Made out' looks like kissing or understanding, but here it means filled in, as with a cheque.
explanation.definitionFit: A cheque or document that has been made out has been filled in by hand, i.e. set down in writing.

clue.text: Crew at sea on King's badly damaged ship

indicators.note: at sea means confused, so the letters are muddled

parts.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: Sailors on a royal vessel that has been badly battered.
explanation.definitionFit: A wreck is a vessel destroyed or ruined, typically by striking rocks.

clue.text: Between exams? No time for hobbies

parts.note: inter- is a prefix meaning between

indicators.note: No says a letter is dropped

parts.note: tests are exams

explanation.surface: A student between exams has no time to pursue pastimes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No' removes T from TESTS, leaving ESTS.
explanation.definitionFit: One's interests are pursuits enjoyed in leisure hours.

clue.text: Tuned car — Tiff's transport

indicators.note: a tuned engine has been adjusted, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: Tiff's car has been tuned up for a drive.
explanation.definitionFit: Traffic means the movement of vehicles or goods, i.e. transport.

clue.text: Native from old city in former African province

indicators.note: in means one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: Natal was a province of South Africa
Ur was an ancient Mesopotamian city

explanation.surface: A local from an ancient city within a vanished African province.
explanation.definitionFit: Native and natural both describe something innate or inborn.

clue.text: Concerned with first bit of chalk, snooker player uses these spares

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held: 'Concerned with first bit of chalk, snooker player uses these spares (7)'. RE + S + CUES, but 'first bit of chalk' gives C, not S; Big Dave's blog calls it a setter's mistake and the website later revised the clue.
annotationWithheld.clue: Concerned with first bit of chalk, snooker player uses these spares

clue.text: Take out former lover, getting caught in Italian restaurant

indicators.note: getting here joins the former partner to the next piece, which follows it

parts.note: an ex is a former partner

indicators.note: in here says the cricket letter goes inside the restaurant's short name

parts.note: a trat is the short form of trattoria, an Italian eatery
C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: An ex-partner turns up at an Italian restaurant, perhaps for a dinner date.
explanation.walkthrough: TRAT (short for trattoria) is a crossword staple; 'getting caught in' puts C inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To extract something is to draw or pull it out, as with a tooth.

clue.text: What Lady Godiva was on, bare — shock spread

indicators.note: spread means the letters are scattered and laid out afresh

explanation.surface: Lady Godiva's naked ride caused shock that spread through Coventry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spread' rearranges BARE SHOCK. Lady Godiva legendarily rode naked through Coventry on a horse.
explanation.definitionFit: Godiva rode through the town mounted on a horse, so she was seated astride it.

clue.text: Point both ways

indicators.note: both ways says the word reads identically forwards and backwards

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.definitionFit: To point someone to a source is to direct them there, a verb sense meaning direct.

clue.text: Joanna's wine almost filled by adult

indicators.note: filled by means a piece goes inside the shortened word
almost means the word is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: pinot is a grape and wine, as in pinot noir
A is the old film-rating abbreviation for adult

explanation.surface: Joanna has a glass of wine that an adult nearly finished.
explanation.walkthrough: Joanna is Cockney rhyming slang (Joanna/piano), a British term not in most dictionaries outside the UK.
explanation.definitionFit: In Cockney rhyming slang, a Joanna is the keyboard instrument found in many pubs.

clue.text: Talk about exercises in action

indicators.note: about means the first word goes around the second

parts.note: an oration is a formal talk or speech
PE is physical education, gym exercises

explanation.surface: A speech about fitness training in practice.
explanation.definitionFit: An operation is a military action, as in a campaign.

clue.text: Call Cassius in revolt that's driven us out of Rome?

indicators.note: in revolt suggests rebellion and upheaval, so the letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: the letters to be removed from the pool

explanation.surface: A call for Cassius to lead the uprising that drove the people out of Rome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in revolt' rearranges CALL CASSIUS after 'driven us out' removes U and S. Cassius was one of the conspirators against Julius Caesar.
explanation.definitionFit: Classical refers to ancient Greek and Roman culture, so it describes things belonging to old Rome.

clue.text: Came together and strolled around Sussex regularly

indicators.note: around means the first word wraps the second

parts.note: ambled means strolled

indicators.note: regularly asks for alternate letters, first, third and fifth

explanation.surface: Someone walked around the county of Sussex at a steady pace.
explanation.walkthrough: Sussex is an English county; its alternate letters give SSE.
explanation.definitionFit: When people assemble, they gather or congregate.

clue.text: Mushrooms in furrows

parts.note: taken as written
furrows are lines or wrinkles, creases

explanation.definitionFit: To mushroom is to grow rapidly, a verb sense of expanding fast.

clue.text: It should cut one's fare

parts.note: reads like a ticket discount, but fare is food, so it is a front tooth for biting

explanation.definitionFit: This sharp front tooth slices food when one bites.

clue.text: Act together to frame MP's brief

indicators.note: to frame means to surround something

parts.note: to coact is to act together
MP is a member of parliament

explanation.surface: A plan for joint action to set up a member of parliament.
explanation.definitionFit: Compact means concise or short, a synonym for brief.

clue.text: Plant's small advantage

parts.note: S is the clothing-size abbreviation for small
an edge is a slight advantage over someone

explanation.surface: A gardener's claim that one plant has a slight lead over its rivals.
explanation.definitionFit: Sedge is a grass-like marsh plant of the genus Carex.

clue.text: At night it's easy to spot and follow celebrity

definitions.text: At night it's easy to spot

parts.note: to dog is to follow closely
a star is a celebrity

explanation.surface: An evening tip that a famous person is easy to tail.
explanation.definitionFit: Sirius, the brightest star in the night sky, is plainly visible after dark.

clue.text: A red mixed with spirit — it pulsates in one's head

indicators.note: mixed means the letters are combined in a new order

parts.note: rum is a spirit

explanation.surface: A red wine mixed with spirit gives one a throbbing head.
explanation.definitionFit: The tympanic membrane vibrates with sound inside the ear.

clue.text: Smallest break in sentence, in fact?

definitions.text: Smallest break in sentence, in fact?

parts.words: Smallest break in sentence, in fact?
parts.note: reads like a prisoner getting the briefest time off a jail term, but means the lightest pause in a written sentence

explanation.definitionFit: This punctuation mark signals the shortest pause within a written sentence.

clue.text: Fast food grub her ma cooked

indicators.note: cooked means the letters are prepared afresh, rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone's mother cooks a meal of quick grub.
explanation.definitionFit: A beef patty in a bun is a staple dish of quick-service outlets.

clue.text: Something perhaps in garden shed gets trapped

indicators.note: trapped says the letters are caught inside the words

explanation.surface: Something in the garden shed becomes stuck.
explanation.definitionFit: A hedge is a boundary of shrubs typically found in a garden.

clue.text: In darkness, Cuban dance queen moves

indicators.note: moves says that letter is shifted elsewhere in the word

parts.note: the rumba is a Cuban dance
R is the abbreviation for regina, queen

explanation.surface: In the dark, a Cuban dancer queen takes to the floor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moves' shifts R from the front of RUMBA to give UMBRA.
explanation.definitionFit: Umbra is the darkest part of a shadow.

clue.text: Upset as bride makes booby, perhaps

indicators.note: upset means knocked over, so the letters are tipped into a new order

explanation.surface: A bride is so distressed that she acts like a fool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upset' rearranges AS BRIDE. 'booby' looks like a fool, but it is a tropical gannet-like bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The booby is a tropical gannet, an example of an ocean-going bird.

clue.text: Fisherman's catch? Throw rest out

parts.note: to lob is to throw something in a high arc

indicators.note: out means the letters are put out of order

explanation.surface: Instructions to toss the remainder of the haul back into the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: This crustacean is landed in pots by fishermen, an example of a sea catch.

clue.text: Regret holding European money for entourage

indicators.note: holding means the first word wraps around the others

parts.note: to rue is to regret
tin is old slang for money

explanation.surface: Someone regrets keeping euros to pay a celebrity's hangers-on.
explanation.definitionFit: A retinue is a group of attendants accompanying an important person, like an entourage.

clue.text: Figure beginning to diet — one with a little weight

indicators.note: beginning to asks for the first letter of the next word

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
taken as written
a gram is a small unit of weight

explanation.surface: A dieter's figure starts to change as someone loses a little weight.
explanation.definitionFit: A diagram is a drawn figure, as in a numbered illustration in a book.
